prompt:
Bug report: models that declare their own auto_init exclusions lose primary-key protection.

Mealie's SQLAlchemy models are initialised through the @auto_init() decorator, which copies the incoming keyword data onto the row and skips the keys in its configuration's exclude set. By default that set is {"id"}, so an id in the incoming data never overwrites a primary key. Models with a model_config = ConfigDict(exclude={...}) of their own (foods, groups, households, shopping-list items, ...) are not protected: an id in the data passed to them, or to their nested one-to-many elements on update, is written onto the row.

Find the cause and fix it. Expected: a model's own exclude adds to the default exclusions instead of replacing them. The configuration auto_init resolves for a model class (_get_config(cls) in the decorator's module, an AutoInitConfig) has exclude equal to {"id"} together with the model's own entries ("id" once if the model lists it too); a class without a model_config, or whose model_config sets other keys only (such as get_attr), keeps exclude == {"id"}.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/unit_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 9 minutes).
title: fix: auto_init merges model_config.exclude with default {"id"} instead of replacing it (#8336)
